of or relating to the works of George Orwell (especially his picture of a future totalitarian state)

Resembling the totalitarian political methods decried in the works of writer George Orwell, particularly in the dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four; characterized by use of misleading terminology, propaganda, censorship, surveillance and repression.
ex: “But they soon find out that an enforced equality, without free individualism to temper it, becomes an Orwellian nightmare-version of the workers' paradise, in which ‘all are equal, but some are more equal than others.’”

In an Orwellian manner.

A surname.
Or something else; allows for the existence of an unexpressed alternative to what was said.
used to indicate a paraphrase or the chance of an error in the details of reported speech.
ex: When he hit his finger with the hammer, he said "ouch" or words to that effect.
